dispute_ticket.description: I was charged S$140 for cleaning but my trip was spotless. The receipt he used looks like one I have seen reused. Please look into it.

driver_profile.name: Eddie Soh
driver_profile.fraud_flag_details: Receipt no. CR-20917 (QuickShine Cleaning) was already attached to cleaning claims on two other trips by this driver (RYDE-FS-OLD-1, RYDE-FS-OLD-2), both paid out in September 2026.

app_events.details: Claim S$140 with receipt CR-20917 (QuickShine Cleaning, dated 2026-10-06).
Receipt number CR-20917 matches receipts on 2 earlier paid claims by driver D-9300.

cleaning_fee_max.text: The maximum cleaning fee in SGD that may be charged to a rider for one trip.

value: cleaning company receipt with name, contact, address and date
cleaning_claim_evidence_required.text: Evidence a driver must provide to support a cleaning fee claim against a rider. It governs driver cleaning claims only.

fraud_check_hit_requires_human_review.text: Governs claims where an automated fraud check matches evidence to earlier claims. A true value means a person must decide; the system does not rule on the claim.

expected_outcome.reason: The claim looks complete (2 photos at 19:24:10 and 19:24:50, five minutes after drop-off at 19:19:00, and a receipt for S$140.00), but the driver profile carries 2 fraud flags and the 'fraud_check_hit' event says receipt no. CR-20917 was already used on two earlier paid claims by the same driver. The rider says her trip was spotless. A reused receipt is a fraud signal, and this trip's policy says such a hit must be decided by a person, so the case is escalated and no refund figure is set.
